axis: a considerate gesture → an act of open-hearted good will

members.tone: The plain warm name for the deed itself, with none of the ceremony *benignity* puts around the same act.
Formal and elevated, praising a kind act at a slight remove where *kindness* simply names it.
Credit for regard paid to someone else — the kindness lies in the care taken, not in warmth as such.
British spelling; the kindness is graciously bestowed, tilting downward from giver to receiver in a way *kindness* does not.
Excusing granted with weight and formality, where *forgiveness* is the same release given personally.
The broadest praise here, naming the good will driving the act as much as the act, whether the kindness lands or is only meant.
Warmer and more inward than *pardon* for the same excusing — a wrong let go rather than officially remitted.
The kindness comes as something granted graciously, which leaves the receiver holding an obligation *consideration* never creates.
Praises the noticing behind the deed, where *consideration* praises the regard the deed shows.
The most openly tender of these, since the act is affection displayed rather than care measured out.
